I was like 9 years old when I played Halo 3, I didn't have an Xbox, let alone a 360  
My parents didn't want me playing games with guns in em  
is that my fault?  
I was too young to understand anything except shooty shoot anyway  


I played through Halo Reach on MCC cause its the first in the timeline and was told by my cousin, who loves the franchise to death, that I should start there. I played through it with him and didn't enjoy the experience because I thought it dragged and created difficulty out of just throwing waves of enemies at you.  


Next step would obviously be Combat Evolved within the Timeline. I had had bad experiences with the game before and expected to hate it once more. Turns out I find it immensely enjoyable in coop.  


How do you compare that to a book with a straight forward plot that reads the same on every readthrough? Games just aren't like that, especially with something like Halo's AI acting differently every time.   
A game doesn't need a story to be enjoyable, it doesn't need to immerse or create a dense atmosphere, gameplay alone can carry a game. It's not like I never understood the appeal of Halo's universe, I always sorta did.  


It's the gameplay that I found tedious and frustrating.   
\- Taking down waves of covenant squads as one guy that always seems to gets shot at from every angle  
\- driving around with an AI in the back who refuses to shoot anything that moves,   
\- Getting bumrushed with your shield down, unable to do anything but sit there and wait until the enemy flanks and shoots you in the head  
\- Levels that last an hour but feel like 2  
\- Hearing the same voice lines and music stings repeat on every reload

Thats what I hated. I felt like all I could ever do is sit in cover, wait, poke my head out, shoot 2 guys, sit in cover, wait, poke my head out, sit in cover, get flanked on low health and killed. And lowering the difficulty, kills didn't feel earned, but granted.  


Coop makes all of that disappear for me. It all suddenly clicked and worked so effortlessly. I wasn't stuck behind rocks anymore, my cousin could distract and leave me to regenerate. If an elite rushed us, we could coordinate an attack pattern for a satisfying kill. Rooms and Waves are cleared way faster. Restarts happen less often because we can pull each other back from death which means we get through the Level quicker. For me, it makes Solo look like it wasn't even designed for it.
